paragraphs.text: Dear elders and sisters, it is a beautiful day. Rain and sunshine all on the same day. Classic Filipino weather. I love it.

All right, we have a few updates to share. Number one, the First Presidency issued some very important principles about how we can handle the challenging times like we're in right now. The document should have arrived in your email today. Let me know if you didn't get it. Read it and become familiar with the principles in it.

The key is understanding principles, methods and strategies. There's millions of those, but if you can get the principles, which is what the First Presidency is teaching us, you understand how to apply them in a million different ways.

Number two, the science is getting more and more clear on this coronavirus. Three new things the scientists have learned. First, that the virus is killed very quickly in bright sunshine. Second, it doesn't live very long in hot temperatures. And third, it doesn't live long in high humidity.
Sounds like we live in the perfect place for avoiding the virus, but still be washing your hands often and when you go out wear the mask and maintain that two meter distance from others.

Number three, there's a good chance that the restrictions on our lockdown are going to get tougher before they get looser. We've done a mission-wide inventory to make sure you have your 14-day supply of food. It sounds like you're all in pretty good shape. Let's keep it that way.

As long as you can buy food in the market, then buy it and eat that food, saving your emergency supply for when you can't get out to buy food. This strategy will keep us safe from losing too much weight in the lockdown. Dieting by starvation is a really bad strategy. I shouldn't joke about that, but I want you to keep your supply on hand.

Number four, eat well, but not too much. I have noticed that some of us are getting a little bigger than we used to be and I'm looking at myself in the mirror when I say that. I am sure that it's not from exercising as much as we used to do.

If you think about it, especially you missionaries, you were out and moving. I mean you'd walk five, ten kilometers a day sometimes and you're not getting that movement now and if you're still eating the same amount, you're going to be putting on weight in all the places you don't want it.
So there's a couple of things we can do about that. Number one, I have plenty of LC and I'm totally willing to deliver some to each apartment who wants it and will use it in place of a meal.

So in other words, you take the LC, you mix it up in your shaker cup and that's your breakfast or that's your dinner or that's your lunch and then you eat two other regular meals and if you do that, you're going to find yourself dropping some fat and that's going to be good.

The other thing you can do is get some more sunshine. The fact of the matter is that's going to help you keep your immune system a lot stronger and that's going to be also something that's going to help you sleep a lot better and believe it or not, getting good sleep actually causes you to burn more fat.

Now another thing you can do is exercise a couple of times a day. Don't be crazy about it. Don't exercise crazy hard. That doesn't actually do you that much good, but move, move, move and move some more.
Never sit longer than an hour. Set a one hour timer on your phone and whenever it goes off, get up and move around for about five minutes.

If you do that, you will speed up your metabolism even more and you'll basically burn fat all day long because the metabolism gets set based upon what you're doing for about an hour and a half or two hours and if you're sitting for about an hour and a half or two hours, the metabolism slows right down because it figures you don't need to burn any fat because you're not doing anything.

So just be constantly getting up, walking around, do some push-ups, do some set-ups, do some jumping jacks. Just move yourself around for about five, 10 minutes and then you can sit back down and get studying again or get back engaged in your work. All right, that's all we've got for the updates.

Let's talk about smooth stone number one. Remember the young shepherd boy David killed a 10-foot giant warrior by using just one smooth stone, but when he was getting ready to go to battle with Goliath, he actually selected five smooth stones just to be ready for anything.
He had proven to himself that he could handle the lions and the wolves with the slingshot and those smooth stones and he knew with the Lord's help he could also handle Goliath, which he in fact did.
So he proved those stones, he proved that strategy and I've proven my own five smooth stones and I'll share all of them with you in the next few days.
But for this afternoon evening, we'll talk about smooth stone number one, which is vision and goals. In Proverbs 29, 18, we read where there is no vision, the people perish.

And we see this on all levels of life. We see it in missionary service and we see it in the business world. We see it at a family level and at a personal level. Without a vision, people just struggle to be motivated. They struggle to get themselves up in the morning. They struggle whenever they have some little negative thing that happens, they fall apart because they don't have this vision.
But when there is a vision, a clear and compelling vision, when that vision is refined and reinforced with emotional and sensory detail, then people get really, really effective.
They just become different and you can see it in someone's face when they've got a vision. They're animated. They have power. There's a magnetism associated with them.

A person that's actuated by this kind of vision is incredibly powerful and attractive, really magnetic to both people and to the resources that they need in order for the vision to become physical, to become real.
Now, I can show you how to make your vision compelling and clear. I can show you how to make it sensory rich and emotionally laden. But you must first find or create the basic vision.

Now, this is not some idle dream. I want to be on the NBA or I want to be when whatever that idle show is, the singing show. It's not something like that. It's got to be something you are actually intensely interested in doing and being.

We talked about this in our message on the five steps. When you choose that big and important goal, it has to be something really important to you. Turning that goal into a vision is a whole different process.

Like I said, I can show you how, but first you need to come up with the big and important goal. And if you do come up with a big and important goal to yourself and you can write it out and make it clear and send it to me, I will show you how to turn it into a clear and compelling vision.
I will show you how to make it emotionally laden and sensory rich, which will help you achieve it. So once you have your vision, what do you do?

Well, first thing you're going to do is commit to a step by step plan on how you're going to move along the path to the fulfillment of your vision. Now, that process is not something I can teach you in an audio message, but I can give you some clues.
First, you got to answer four questions. And here are the questions. What, what do you really want? Two, why, why do you want it? Three, what again? What will you sacrifice to get it?

This is important because this is the thing. You got to, you got to leave first base to get to second base. If you're, if you're going to discover a new island, you've got to leave the island that you're on right now. You've got to give up something in order to get what you want.
And so that sacrifice really tells it tells heaven. It tells God that you're serious about this. Now, all of us have got things that we probably ought to give up anyway.

And sometimes we can go to the Lord and we can say, I'm willing to sacrifice this bad habit or this thing that I'm doing that's not very productive. If, if, if you, if you will help me, Heavenly Father, get this thing that I really want. So that's what I'm talking about when I say, what will you sacrifice to get it?
Fourth, when, and this is a double, when will you start and when do you want to get it? So establishing how I'm starting now today, I'm not even going to wait till tomorrow. I'm starting now.

But the next when is, when do you want to get it? And you need to project yourself out there in the future and look out there and say, in three years, I want to have this degree in this field. I want to have this home. I want to be driving this car. I want to have this, this profession.
And you, you establish a dateline that says, by this time, I will be, I will do, I will have this goal achieved.

After you've had the answers to those questions satisfied, you need to create a statement. Literally, you need to write a screenplay of what life will be like for you when you've accomplished the goal, when the vision has gone from being in your head to in the real world.
Once you have that screenplay, that statement written out, you need to spend about 10 to 15 minutes twice a day just meditating, just visualizing this screenplay happening to you now.
We call this seeing with the eye of faith, seeing something that's not yet real as if it is real, seeing something that's not yet done as if it is already done.

Prophet Joseph Smith said, and he was really good at this, faith was mental exertion, not physical force. Faith operates in the mental arena outside of the physical or what we'd say in philosophy, it's the metaphysical.

As you exercise and discipline your mind, you in effect are exercising your faith. When you have a clear vision in your mind and you can discipline your mind to hold that vision consistently throughout the day, the vision will become real to you in your mind and gradually it will become more and more physically real to you in the actual world.

Holding something in your mind is hard though. We have lots of distractions and the world is constantly trying to get us off of our focus. Many people can't stop themselves from being distracted with everything that comes across their senses. They smell something, they see something, they hear something, they're gone.
These people are like human butterflies unable to concentrate on their goal and so it never becomes real for them and they live a life that's so far below their potential is just tragic.

As the prophet Joseph said, faith is mental exertion. We have to work at it. We might call it mental focus. We have to develop the muscle of being able to focus on something, to concentrate on something.

Sister Lau in her workshop with Sister Ancahas talked a lot about what her mother says, concentrate, concentrate. Her mother's a wise woman because building the skill of concentration is most of the battle of life.

Literally when you can keep your focus on the fulfillment of your goal, you'll be 90% done with that goal. It will happen and so as the Bible says, with faith you can move a mountain and you can achieve any really important goal too.

That's enough for today. On Monday we'll discuss smooth stone number two. Enjoy the rest of your day, make it productive and always remember that we love you and we are so very proud of you. Good night.
